mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically different from a flat baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that amplifies wage growth and input costs, compressing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.10), or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (> 5% CPIAUCSL).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) contraction of more than 1% signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not robust during periods of strong demand growth (GDPC1 q/q > 1.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in CPIAUCSL of more than 1 percentage point year-over-year signals a deflationary easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.05), or the effect reverses when unemployment rises above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% m/m) combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% month-over-month signals strengthening household demand, which supports corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m change > 0.5% AND HOUST m/m change > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent when inflation exceeds 4% (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.0% for four consecutive months signals a structurally tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.05), or the effect is reversed when GDP growth (GDPC1 q/q) exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply expansion, which typically coincides with higher earnings and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change > 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when demand proxies (GDPC1 q/q) are contracting.
